summary.oneLiner: Owns and operates Hyatt Regency Kolkata, a star hotel serving business, MICE and social/wedding travellers in the Kolkata hospitality market.
summary.business: Asian Hotels (East) Limited owns and operates Hyatt Regency Kolkata under the Hyatt brand, serving business travellers, MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions) groups, sports blocks and social/wedding guests. The Company has two wholly-owned, unlisted subsidiaries, Novak Hotels Private Limited (developing a hotel project in Mumbai) and GJS Hotels Limited (a non-operational entity in Odisha), and reports no change in the nature of its business since incorporation.

currentContext.strengths: Hyatt brand affiliation supports demand from corporate, MICE and wedding segments|Agile channel/business-mix management (brand.com and online distributors for high-priced demand, traditional corporate for base business, and group business from weddings, corporate MICE and sports blocks) helped ADR grow 9.8% for the hotel in FY26|Ended FY26 ranked 2 in Revenue per Available Room (RevPAR) among its competitive set despite low market demand, and improved market share
currentContext.strategies: Securing mid-size business groups and larger social gatherings to retain market share, catching up to the trend of strong demand from large MICE events|Diversifying offerings, particularly in the social and events segment, to mitigate seasonal variations and capture evolving consumer preferences|Addressing talent shortage, investing in product upgrades and strengthening brand positioning to sustain competitiveness in a dynamic market|Agile business-mix management across brand.com/online distributors (high-priced demand), traditional corporate (base business), and group business (weddings, corporate MICE and sports blocks)|The Board did not recommend a dividend for FY26, prioritising conservation of cash resources to meet the Company's own capex requirements and to provide financial support to wholly-owned subsidiary Novak Hotels Pvt Ltd as and whenever required; the promoter has assured to infuse funds into Novak Hotels as needed to address the erosion of its net worth, which management views as temporary.
currentContext.expansion: Wholly-owned subsidiary Novak Hotels Private Limited commenced renovation/refurbishment work during FY26 at the Hyatt Regency Mumbai hotel project site; management expects to start hotel operations there in the future, with no specific timeline disclosed. The Company itself continued to conserve cash to meet its own (unspecified) capex requirements at Hyatt Regency Kolkata and to support Novak Hotels as and whenever required.
currentContext.mdna: Kolkata's star hotel industry showed steady resilience in FY26 with occupancy of 71.8% (up 2.7% YoY) despite a softer Q4 driven by fewer auspicious wedding dates|Average Daily Rate (ADR) for the Kolkata star hotel industry grew a strong 8.5% YoY, underscoring the industry's pricing power even amid seasonal fluctuations, supported by demand across business and leisure segments|Social and wedding tourism moderated during the year, but leisure and business travel remained resilient, supported by improved connectivity and rising domestic demand|Outlook remains encouraging: limited supply, strengthening ADR and Kolkata's expanding appeal as a cultural and commercial destination are expected to sustain growth momentum|Competition is intensifying from newly renovated and new hotels with modern amenities, and from the expansion of international hotel chains across eastern India, particularly threatening the business-travel segment

risks.risk: High attrition and scarcity of skilled hospitality talent
risks.note: Flagged as the most pressing threat for the Kolkata star hotel sector; uncertain job-market conditions and evolving career preferences make it difficult to attract and retain the right professionals, expected to persist over the next couple of years and potentially affect service quality and operational efficiency.

risks.risk: Intensifying local competition from new and renovated properties
risks.note: Newly renovated properties and new hotels entering the Kolkata market with updated products and modern amenities pose a significant threat to established hotels, particularly in capturing the business-travel segment.

risks.risk: Expansion of international hotel chains across eastern India
risks.note: Growing distribution of global hotel brands across eastern India, including Kolkata, is creating heightened competition at multiple price points and locations, requiring local operators to differentiate to retain both business and leisure travellers.
The Company's operating performance is derived from a single hotel, Hyatt Regency Kolkata, making results highly sensitive to demand, competitive and event-calendar conditions in one city/market.

risks.risk: Seasonality of demand, particularly wedding/social tourism
risks.note: A softer Q4 was driven largely by fewer auspicious wedding dates versus the prior year, and the social/wedding tourism segment moderated during the year, illustrating the Company's exposure to seasonal and event-calendar variation.

Wholly-owned subsidiary GJS Hotels Ltd's Odisha government revocation order remains under a High Court stay with the matter pending further hearing and no date yet listed, an unresolved regulatory overhang on that asset.
